direct_answer: BASF integrates sustainability-related performance into incentive schemes primarily through (1) the long-term incentive (LTI) for the Board of Executive Directors and senior executives and (2) a short-term incentive (STI) program for senior executives in operating business units. BASF anchored the reduction of Group-wide CO2 emissions (Scope 1 and Scope 2) as “the most important nonfinancial key performance indicator” in its steering and compensation systems in 2020; this CO2 reduction KPI is one of three equally weighted strategic targets (33.3%) in the LTI for the Board of Executive Directors and senior executives [Source 2]. For the STI introduced for senior executives in operating business units in the reporting year, BASF includes three non-financial targets (occupational and process safety; sustainability; development of the operating divisions) that together account for 25% of the STI formula; the first two are sustainability-related, meaning 16.7% of the entire STI formula is sustainability-related [Source 2]. BASF states that the “entire STI formula is sustainability-related,” and specifies that the STI sustainability target includes elements contributing to its green transformation, such as sales of Sustainable-Future Solutions and increasing the share of purchased raw materials with supplier-specific Product Carbon Footprints [Source 1][Source 2]. BASF also discloses that Supervisory Board remuneration has no variable components and is therefore not linked to target achievement [Source 2].
compliance_rationale: BASF discloses key characteristics of sustainability integration in incentives (LTI and STI), identifies specific sustainability-related targets/metrics (Scope 1&2 CO2 reduction; occupational/process safety; sustainability target elements such as Sustainable-Future Solutions sales and supplier-specific PCFs), and quantifies the proportion of variable remuneration linked to sustainability for both LTI (33.3%) and STI (16.7%) [Source 2][Source 1]. However, the retrieved passages do not provide the ESRS 2 GOV-3-required information on the level at which incentive scheme terms are approved and updated, nor do they fully describe how sustainability metrics are embedded in remuneration policies beyond the stated KPIs/targets [Source 2].
disclosure_gaps: Level in the undertaking at which the terms of the incentive schemes are approved and updated (e.g., which body/committee approves/updates LTI/STI terms) is not provided in the retrieved passages (ESRS 2 GOV-3(e)).

Further detail on how sustainability-related performance metrics are used as performance benchmarks or included in remuneration policies (beyond naming the KPIs/targets and weights) is not provided in the retrieved passages (ESRS 2 GOV-3(c)).

Clarification/consistency on the statement that the “entire STI formula is sustainability-related” versus the quantified 16.7% sustainability-related share is not explained in the retrieved passages [Source 1][Source 2].

Coverage for administrative/management bodies beyond the Board of Executive Directors and specified senior executives (e.g., other administrative/management roles) is not evidenced in the retrieved passages (scope clarity).
key_findings: Scope 1 and Scope 2 CO2 emissions reduction is the most important nonfinancial KPI in BASF’s steering and compensation systems and is a 33.3% weighted strategic target in the LTI for the Board of Executive Directors and senior executives [Source 2].
Supervisory Board remuneration has no variable components and is not linked to sustainability target achievement [Source 2].

STI for senior executives in operating business units includes three equally weighted non-financial targets (25% of STI formula); two are sustainability-related, resulting in 16.7% of the STI formula being sustainability-related [Source 2].

STI sustainability target elements include sales of Sustainable-Future Solutions and increasing the share of purchased raw materials with supplier-specific Product Carbon Footprints [Source 1][Source 2].
